clue.text: Gym l-leaked, having wood surface on exterior walls

parts.note: PE, physical education, is school gym
the stammered spelling copies its first letter, so a stuttered 'bled' (leaked) is B-BLED
ash is a kind of tree and its timber

explanation.surface: A gym sprang a leak, and it has a wooden facing on the outside walls.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in 'l-leaked' mimics a stammer; apply the same stutter to its synonym BLED to get BBLED.
explanation.definitionFit: Pebbledash is a rendering of mortar studded with small stones, used to coat outside walls of houses.

clue.text: Speed and power that comes with unreturnable service

parts.note: P is the physics abbreviation for power
in tennis an ace is a serve the opponent cannot return

explanation.surface: Speed and power go with a serve that cannot be returned in tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: Pace is a plain synonym for speed or rate of movement.

clue.text: British worker eats what in Paris? Not petit déjeuner!

indicators.note: one piece eating another takes it inside itself, so the worker swallows the French word

parts.note: the ant is the crossword's stock worker insect
que is French for 'what'

explanation.surface: A British labourer eats something, but whatever it is, it is no small French breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is playful: petit déjeuner is French for breakfast, a small meal, and the answer is the opposite, a lavish feast.
explanation.definitionFit: A banquet is a grand formal feast, the very opposite of a light continental breakfast.

clue.text: Dealer Gareth, surprisingly generous

indicators.note: the letters are rearranged in a surprising way, signalling a reshuffle of the two names

explanation.surface: A card dealer named Gareth turns out, unexpectedly, to be a kind and giving man.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with a big heart is kind and openhanded, which is what generous means.

clue.text: Set aside time in which dice can be played

indicators.note: the time word holds the shuffled dice within it

parts.note: a date is a point in time

indicators.note: dice played are thrown and land in a new order, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Reserve a time slot during which a game of dice can be enjoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set aside' reads like the start of an instruction but is the definition; 'can be played' scrambles the dice to EDIC, which 'in which' sets within the time word.
explanation.definitionFit: To dedicate something is to devote or reserve it for a particular purpose, i.e. set it aside.

clue.text: Scoundrel in Durham, say, establishing firm

indicators.note: the scoundrel sits inside the bishop's seat word

parts.note: Durham is an example of a see, a bishop's diocese
a cur is a contemptible man

explanation.surface: A rogue in the city of Durham is setting up a company.
explanation.walkthrough: Durham is an English cathedral city and diocese; 'firm' looks like a company noun but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Secure as an adjective means fixed and steady, which is firm.

clue.text: Such oats regularly provided for northerner

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the two words

explanation.surface: Oats like these are supplied for someone from the north, porridge being a Scottish staple.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Scotland lives in the far north of Britain, so is a northerner.

clue.text: American university room housing little old sailors

indicators.note: the room word houses, or contains, the other pieces

parts.note: a cell is a small room, as in a monastery or prison
O is a short form of old
RN is the Royal Navy, i.e. sailors

explanation.surface: A college in the USA has a room where some elderly seamen are lodged.
explanation.definitionFit: Cornell is an Ivy League university in Ithaca, New York state.

clue.text: The circle leading revolution is speculating

indicators.note: leading puts the first pieces in front of the next one

parts.note: O is circle-shaped
a rising is a revolt or uprising

explanation.surface: The group at the centre of the revolt is busy hypothesising.
explanation.definitionFit: Theorising is forming theories, conjecturing about something: speculating.

clue.text: Little female in agreement or dispute?

indicators.note: the girl's name goes inside the agreement word

parts.note: a contract is a binding agreement
Di is a short form of the woman's name Diana

explanation.surface: Is a young girl going along with things, or arguing?
explanation.definitionFit: To contradict is to deny or argue against what someone says, i.e. dispute it.

clue.text: Lake is weird, one end being invisible

indicators.note: one end letter of the synonym disappears from view, a deletion

parts.note: eerie means strange and unsettling

explanation.surface: A lake is strange, with one of its shores out of sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Erie is one of the Great Lakes of North America.

clue.text: Small digit — five?

definitions.meaning: the smallest finger of the hand, the pinkie
anatomically the fifth digit of the hand, counting from the thumb

explanation.definitionFit: The pinkie is the smallest finger and is numbered the fifth digit of the hand.

clue.text: Priest brings healing

definitions.meaning: in France, the clergyman in charge of a parish
a remedy or restoration to health

explanation.definitionFit: Curé is a French parish priest; a cure is also a remedy that brings healing.

clue.text: Soldier turning writer in profession

indicators.note: the turned writer goes inside the profession word

parts.note: a career is one's profession

indicators.note: turning means the writing implement word is read backwards

parts.note: a nib is the writing point of a pen

explanation.surface: A soldier is switching to a writing profession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' turns the pen point backwards to BIN; 'in' lodges it within the profession word, so the soldier is not literally changing jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: A carbineer is a soldier armed with a carbine, a short rifle.

clue.text: Community payment

definitions.meaning: a village or colony where people have settled
the paying of a bill or the sum paid to resolve a claim

explanation.definitionFit: A settlement is both a place people have settled and the clearing of an account.

clue.text: Request to put shovel down in gateway?

indicators.note: the eating word goes into the gateway word

parts.note: an entry is a way in or entrance
to shovel food down is slang for eating

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to lay a spade down in an entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put shovel down' reads as laying a spade aside but means to shovel food down, i.e. eat.
explanation.definitionFit: An entreaty is an earnest plea, a request.

clue.text: Stands and procrastinates

explanation.definitionFit: Stalls are stands at a market, and someone who stalls delays to avoid acting.

clue.text: Nasty ailments one gets in underground working environment

indicators.note: nasty suggests the letters are turned into a horrid jumble, an anagram signal

explanation.surface: Nasty illnesses you pick up while toiling below ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface hints at miners' illnesses, which fits the answer's scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A salt mine is an underground workplace where rock salt is extracted.

clue.text: Stop that article going out about war

indicators.note: about means the trimmed word goes around the conflict word
going out means the article leaves the word that

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
taken as written

explanation.surface: Stop that newspaper piece being published about the conflict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going out' drops the article from 'that', leaving THT, and 'about' says those letters surround the conflict word; 'Stop' at the front is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To thwart a plan is to block or prevent it, so stop it.

clue.text: Little ring being accepted? That's wonderful!

indicators.note: a ring being accepted is taken inside the small word

parts.note: wee is Scots for little
a hoop is a ring

explanation.surface: A small ring is taken, and the reaction is delight.
explanation.definitionFit: Whoopee is an exclamation of joy or excitement, like 'great!'

clue.text: These reps could be nameless

indicators.note: could be says the fodder's letters could form another word

explanation.surface: Sales representatives might be anonymous people.
explanation.definitionFit: Reps, short for representatives, are salesmen who sell goods for a firm.

clue.text: Actor Roger has pocketed one old penny and gold coin

indicators.note: pocketed means taken inside, so the actor's surname holds the other pieces

parts.note: Roger Moore was the actor who played James Bond
I is the Roman numeral one
D was the symbol for the pre-decimal British penny

explanation.surface: Roger Moore has slipped a single penny and a gold coin into his pocket.
explanation.walkthrough: Before 1971, British pennies were written d (from Latin denarius).
explanation.definitionFit: A moidore was an old Portuguese gold coin, also current in England in the 18th century.

clue.text: Seize Greek character with commotion around

indicators.note: around puts the commotion word on either side of the Greek letter

parts.note: din is a loud noise or disturbance
eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: Arrest a Greek person surrounded by uproar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' suggests a person from Greece but is a letter of its alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: To detain is to hold or take into custody, i.e. seize.

clue.text: Escape from habitat in which there's nothing quiet

indicators.note: the habitat word has the other pieces within it

parts.note: one's element is one's natural environment
O is zero, nothing
P is piano, the musical marking for quiet

explanation.surface: Breaking out of a living space where all is totally silent.
explanation.definitionFit: An elopement is running away secretly to marry, an escape from one's family.

clue.text: Bit of an eye for a girl

definitions.meaning: the coloured ring around the pupil

explanation.definitionFit: The iris is part of the eye; Iris is also a girl's name.

clue.text: Involvement in celebration cut short

indicators.note: cut short means the last letter is lopped off

parts.note: a party is a celebration

explanation.surface: Joining in at a celebration that ends early.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a part in something means being involved in it, so part means involvement.

clue.text: Spot extremists in Etonian's party

indicators.note: the extremists are the outermost letters of each of the two words

explanation.surface: Pick out the radicals at an Eton pupil's party.
explanation.walkthrough: An Etonian is a pupil at Eton College, the English public school.
explanation.definitionFit: To espy is to catch sight of, which is to spot.

clue.text: Flexible bag is OK and gets used in the kitchen

indicators.note: flexible signals letters bending into a new shape

explanation.surface: A bendy bag is fine and gets put to use while cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is part of the anagram fodder, not a joining word.
explanation.definitionFit: Bicarbonate of soda is a raising agent for baking cakes and bread in the kitchen.

clue.text: Beat down group by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it signals a word that sounds like the synonym

parts.note: a team is a group working together

explanation.surface: Defeat a group, from what one hears.
explanation.definitionFit: Rain that beats down heavily teems, i.e. pours.

clue.text: Tender name contrived to convey affection

indicators.note: contrived means artificially arranged, signalling a reordering of the letters

explanation.surface: A soft nickname is invented to show fondness.
explanation.definitionFit: An endearment is a word or act expressing affection, such as a pet name.
